Bookkeeping questions from local business owners

Yes — that's a normal part of the monthly close. Card processors pay out days later, bundled, and net of their fees, so a bank deposit is almost never one day's sales. Your bookkeeper ties the payouts back to the sales that earned them and records the fees as their own cost.

Yes. Your income and the costs that go with it get grouped by what you sell — services one side, retail the other, or however you split food and drinks, cleaning and alterations, treatments and packages. Your bookkeeper sets those groups up with you at the start using the words you already use.

A gift card is money you're holding, not money you've earned — you still owe the service. Your bookkeeper records it that way and moves it into your income as it gets redeemed, so a strong December of gift card sales doesn't look like a strong December of profit.

Tips are recorded separately from wages, so your payroll line reflects what the business actually paid out and what simply passed through to your staff. Bench doesn't run your payroll — a payroll provider does that, and Bench reconciles it.
No. Keep ringing sales through whatever you use now. Bench bookkeepers can also work inside your existing QuickBooks account if that's what you'd prefer.
